blocks.title: Introduction( Locomotion and Movement )
blocks.text:
Movement :- One of the significant features of both plants and animals.

Locomotion :- Voluntary movements which results in change in place or location. Walking, running, climbing, flying, swimming are all some forms of locomotory movements.

  • Locomotion  is generally for search of food, shelter, mating, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic condition and escapes from enemies/predators.
  • All locomotions are movements but all movements are not locomotion.
  • Method of locomotion performed by animals vary with their habitats and demand of situation.
  • Locomotory structure need not be different from those affecting other type of movements like Hydra can use its tentacles for capturing of prey and also use them for locomotion.

blocks.title: Question. 1
blocks.question:
Cells of human body does not exhibit which of the following type of movement?

(1) Flagellated

(2) Ciliary

(3) Muscular

(4) Amoeboid
blocks.answer:
Answer = 1

Flagellated movement: This type of movement is driven by flagella, which are whip-like appendages that can propel cells. While flagella are present in certain human cells (e.g., sperm cells), they are not found in the majority of human body cells.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Which filamentous proteins are found in muscle?

(1) Leucine & myosin protein

(2) Actin & myosin protein

(3) Actin & leucine protein

(4) Actin protein only
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

  • Actin and myosin are the two primary filamentous proteins found in muscle fibers, playing a key role in muscle contraction.
  • Actin forms the thin filaments.
  • Myosin forms the thick filaments.
blocks.prompt: Which filamentous proteins are found in muscle?

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Myosin head contains :-

(1) ATPase

(2) ATP binding sites

(3) Active sites for actin

(4) All of these
blocks.answer:
Answer = 4

Explanation:

The myosin head contains the following:

  • ATPase: The myosin head has an ATPase activity, meaning it can hydrolyze ATP to ADP and inorganic phosphate (Pi), which provides the energy for muscle contraction.
  • ATP binding sites: The myosin head has binding sites for ATP, which is necessary for the muscle contraction process.
  • Active sites for actin: The myosin head also has active sites that bind to actin, the thin filament, forming cross-bridges during muscle contraction.

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements

Statement I : Each myofibril has alternate dark and light band on it.

Statement II : Myosin filaments are thinner as compared to the actin filaments.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below.

(1) Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect.

(2) Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.

(3) Statement-I is incorrect but statement-II is correct.

(4) Both statement-I and statement-II are correct.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

  • Statement I: "Each myofibril has alternate dark and light band on it."
  • This is correct. Myofibrils consist of repeating units called sarcomeres, and each sarcomere has alternating dark (A band) and light (I band) regions, giving the muscle its striated appearance.
  • Statement II: "Myosin filaments are thinner as compared to the actin filaments."
  • This is incorrect. Myosin filaments (thick filaments) are actually thicker than actin filaments (thin filaments).
options: (1) Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect.
(2) Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.
(3) Statement-I is incorrect but statement-II is correct.
(4) Both statement-I and statement-II are correct.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
According to the sliding filament theory:

(1) Actin and myosin filaments slide over each other to increase the length of the  sarcomere.

(2) Length of A–band does not change.

(3) I–band increases in length

(4) The actin filaments slide away from A–band resulting in shortening of sarcomere.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

  • Sliding filament theory explains the process of muscle contraction, where the actin (thin) and myosin (thick) filaments slide past each other, causing the sarcomere (the functional unit of the muscle) to shorten.
(1) Actin and myosin filaments slide over each other to shorten the sarcomere, not to increase its length. So this statement is incorrect.

(2) The A-band represents the region where myosin filaments are located, and it does not change in length during contraction. This statement is correct.

(3) The I-band (which contains only actin filaments) decreases in length during contraction, not increases. This statement is incorrect.

(4) The actin filaments slide toward the A-band, not away from it, causing the sarcomere to shorten. This statement is incorrect.
options: (1) Actin and myosin filaments slide over each other to increase the length of the  sarcomere.
(2) Length of A–band does not change.
(4) The actin filaments slide away from A–band resulting in shortening of sarcomere.

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Calcium is important in skeletal muscle contraction because it :-

(1) binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.

(2) activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it.

(3) detaches the myosin head from the actin filament.

(4) prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross bridges and the actin filament
blocks.answer:
Answer = 1

Explanation:

  • During muscle contraction, calcium ions (Ca²⁺) play a crucial role. When an action potential reaches the muscle fiber, calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the sarcoplasm. Calcium then binds to troponin, a regulatory protein on the actin filament.
  • This binding causes a conformational change in troponin, which moves tropomyosin (another regulatory protein) away from the active sites on actin. This exposes the active sites, allowing myosin heads to bind to actin, leading to muscle contraction.
options: (1) binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.
(2) activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it.
(3) detaches the myosin head from the actin filament.
(4) prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross bridges and the actin filament

blocks.title: Visceral Muscles and Cardiac Muscles
blocks.text:
• Visceral muscles are located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs of the body like the alimentary canal, reproductive tract, etc. They do not exhibit any striation and are smooth in appearance. Hence, they are called smooth muscles (nonstriated muscle). Their activities are not under the voluntary control of the nervous system and are therefore known as involuntary muscles. They assist, for example, in the transportation of food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract.
  • Cardiac muscles : As the name suggests, Cardiac muscles are the muscles of heart. Many cardiac muscle cells assemble in a branching pattern to form a cardiac muscle. Based on appearance, cardiac muscles are striated. They are involuntary in nature as the nervous system does not control their activities directly.
DISORDERS OF MUSCULAR SYSTEM:

  • Myasthenia gravis: Auto immune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle.
  • Muscular dystrophy:progressive degeneration of skeletal muscles mostly due to genetic disorder.
  • Tetany: Rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Which of the following muscular disorders is inherited?

(1) Tetany

(2) Muscular dystrophy

(3) Myasthenia gravis

(4) Botulism
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

  • Muscular dystrophy is a group of inherited genetic disorders that lead to muscle weakness and degeneration.
blocks.prompt: Which of the following muscular disorders is inherited?

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Which of the following diseases is an autoimmune disorder?

(1) Myasthenia gravis

(2) Arthritis

(3) Osteoporosis

(4) Gout
blocks.answer:
Answer = 1

Explanation:

  • Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder in which the body's immune system attacks and damages the acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, leading to muscle weakness.
blocks.prompt: Which of the following diseases is an autoimmune disorder?

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Which of the following statements wrongly represents the nature of smooth muscle?

(1) These muscle have no striations

(2) They are involuntary muscles

(3) Communication among the cells is performed by intercalated discs

(4) These muscles are present in the wall of blood vessels
blocks.answer:
Answer = 3

Explanation

Communication among the cells is performed by intercalated discs. This is incorrect. Intercalated discs are a feature of cardiac muscle, not smooth muscle.
options: (3) Communication among the cells is performed by intercalated discs
(4) These muscles are present in the wall of blood vessels
